2. According to DAR, on 21.08.2017, the petitioner was going from Sector - 11 to Sector - 7, Rohini,
Delhi on his motorcycle bearing registration no. DL11-SA-0850.

At about 12:00 Noon, when he reached near Near Swarn Jayanti Park Petrol Pump, Sector - 9, Rohini, Delhi, one Van bearing registration no. DL1K-0598 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against the motorcycle of petitioner with a great force, as a result of which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter, petitioner was taken to BSA Hospital, Delhi, where he was medically examined vide MLC No. 11831/17.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 1 himself and the same was uninsured during the period in question.
MACP No. 1016/17; FIR No. 424/17.; PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 03.06.2025 3.
In his written statement, the respondent no.1 i.e., driver-cum- owner has claimed that he has not caused the alleged accident and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further claimed that he was having valid driving licence and permit at the time of accident.
He denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.

4. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 23.04.2018 passed by my Ld. Predecessor:-
1.

Whether the injured Veerpal suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 21.08.2017 at about 12:00 pm, near Swarn Jayanti Park, Petrol Pump, Sector - 9, Rohini, Delhi,
within the jurisdiction of PS. Prashant Vihar due to rashness and negligence on the part of the driver-cum-owner Sachin who was driving vehicle bearing registration no.
DL1K-0598?

sentences.text: The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
18.

These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental Insurance Co,. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-
"10. The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.

sentences.text: Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

sentences.text: The Bill (which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/1 colly) of Jai Hospital & Research Centre filed on record, shows that he was admitted in the said Hospital on 24.08.2017 and was discharged on 05.09.2017.
As per the said bill, the case of petitioner was of comminuted fracture U.E. both bones leg (L) with vascular insufficiency with blisters.
It is also apparent from the OPD Card (which is part of Ex. PW1/3) that the case of petitioner was below knee(Left) amputation.
Apart from aforesaid treatment record, petitioner has failed to file any other treatment record showing the exact period till which he received the treatment.

In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess work in assessing the loss of income.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.

Considering the nature of MACP No. 1016/17; FIR No. 424/17.;
PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 03.06.2025 injuries sustained by the petitioner and his age being 52 years at the time of accident, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work at least for a period of 6 months or so including his recovery period.
26. It may be noted here that no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove monthly income of injured/petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Petitioner has also failed to file his educational qualification documents.
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 13,584/- per month as on the date of accident which is 21.08.2017.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 81,504/- (Rs. 13,584/- x 6) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant/petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
Thus, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of the petitioner.
12. Further, there is no gainsaying that respondent/driver-cum-owner of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.
It has been duly established that petitioner sustained injuries as per his MLC in the road accident which took place on 21.08.2017 at 12:00 PM, Near Swarn Jayanti Park Petrol Pump, Sector - 9,
Rohini, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
Apart from aforesaid treatment record, petitioner has failed to file any other treatment record showing the exact period till which he received the treatment.
In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess work in assessing the loss of income.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.
Considering the nature of MACP No. 1016/17; FIR No. 424/17.;
PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 03.06.2025 injuries sustained by the petitioner and his age being 52 years at the time of accident, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work at least for a period of 6 months or so including his recovery period.
Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
It is settled law that a particular amount cannot be fixed on pain and sufferings for all cases as is varies from case to case.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, duration of treatment and permanent disability suffered by him, a sum of Rs. 1,50,000/- is considered reasonable towards pain & sufferings.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 70% in relation to his left lower limb and there was amputation of left lower limb (below knee).
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.
The petitioner in the present case was stated to be a Contractor at the time of accident.
It is quite obvious that for any profession, proper movement of all the limbs is very necessary.
Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances of the case including the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner as well as the disability and amputation suffered by him, his functional disability is taken as 70% with regard to whole body.
Thus, the petitioner was more than 51 years of age as on the date of accident.
opennyai_summary.issue: 14. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove his case on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, that he sustained injuries in road accident which took place on 21.08.2017 at 12:00 PM, Near Swarn Jayanti Park Petrol Pump, Sector - 9, Rohini, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

Thus, a sum of Rs. 13,80,677.76p is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.
Thus, the total compensation is assessed as under:-
1.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,46,508.34p 2. Loss of income Rs. 81,504/-
3. Pain and suffering Rs. 1,50,000/-
Loss of future income Rs. 13,80,677.76p Total Rs. 19,08,690.10p
Rounded off to Rs. 19,09,000/-
34.
Since, the offending vehicle was uninsured at the time of accident, respondent being driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount to the petitioner.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.
In view of my finding on issues no. 1 & 2, I award a sum of Rs. 19,09,000/- (including interim award amount, if any) alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum w.e.f date of filing the claim petition i.e. 13.12.2017(except for the period of delay w.e.f., 11.03.2020 till 14.09.2022 as petitioner was failed to lead evidence despite grant of sufficient opportunities) till the date of its realization, in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
APPORTIONMENT 36.
Statement of petitioner in terms of Clause 29 MCTAP was recorded on 28.10.2024.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the permanent disability suffered by the petitioner, it is hereby ordered that out of the awarded amount, a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) shall be immediately released to the petitioner through his Bank account no.
110206784865, Canara Bank, Sector - 14, Rohini, Delhi having IFSC Code CNRB0019167 and remaining amount alongwith interest amount be kept in the form of FDRs in the multiples of Rs.
25,000/-each for a period of one month, two months, three months and so on and so forth, having cumulative interest.
Respondent being driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the entire award amount alongwith interest in the aforesaid bank account of the claimant within 30 days as per above order, failing which he shall be liable to pay interest @ 9% p.a for the period of delay.
In view of the above, concerned Manager of petitioner's bank is directed to release only Rs.
5,00,000/- to the petitioner, on completing necessary formalities as per rules.
He is further directed to keep the remaining amount in fixed deposit in terms of aforesaid directions and send compliance report to this Court.
He is also directed to ensure that no loan, advance or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the fixed deposits without permission of the Court.
Copy of this award be given dasti to claimant.
Copy of this award be sent to respondent through SHO, PS. Prashant Vihar for information and compliance.
Petitioner is also directed to provide copy of this award to his/her bank Manager for compliance.
Form XVI & Form XVII in terms of MCTAP are annexed herewith as Annexure-A.
Copy of order be also sent to concerned M.M and DLSA as per clause 31 and 32 of MCTAP.
